newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ten hurt as Manila squatters battle troopers.
newsitem.headline: Ten hurt as Manila squatters battle troopers.

text.p: Ten people were injured on Monday when squatters armed with rocks battled Philippine troops trying to evict them from part of an army reservation sold to private builders, an army spokesman said.
Soldiers and police used water hoses to disperse more than 100 residents who barricaded a road with beds, tree trunks, steel and concrete pipes and burning car tyres.
Three protesters, including a soldier, were arrested and charged with malicious mischief, army spokesman Colonel Antonio Inciong said.
The squatters, numbering about 300, occupy part of the huge military camp in Manila which the government sold in 1995 to a consortium led by Metro Pacific Corp, a unit of Hong Kong's First Pacific
The consortium plans to turn the area into an industrial and commercial complex under a 39.2-billion-peso ($1.5 billion) deal it signed with the government.
The squatters, who include low-ranking soldiers, said they had lived in the area for at least six years and a court order was needed to drive them out.
Demolition teams tore down 18 of the 60 squatter houses after the protesters dispersed and said they would rip down the rest on Tuesday.
